column7: Talk with them directly and supportively to understand the issue and agree on next steps
column8: Report them to the supervisor immediately
column10: A direct, respectful conversation is usually the best first step.

column4: You disagree with the approach your team has chosen. What should you do?
column5: Share your view and reasons, listen to others and support the final team decision
column6: Quietly do it your own way
column10: Raising concerns constructively and then committing to the decision supports team effectiveness.

column4: Your team completes a successful project. Who should receive credit?
column5: The whole team, with specific contributions acknowledged
column10: Sharing credit and acknowledging contributions builds trust and motivation.

column4: In Tuckman's model of team development, which stage comes immediately after 'storming'?
column10: The sequence is forming, storming, norming, performing (and adjourning).

column4: A coworker is overwhelmed with a deadline, and your own work is on track. What is the best action?
column5: Tell the supervisor they are behind
column6: Offer to help with specific tasks
column7: Stay focused only on your work
column10: Offering help when your own work allows supports shared team goals.

column4: What is the best way to keep teammates informed of your progress on shared work?
column5: Update the shared tracker or briefly report status at agreed check-ins
column6: Send long daily emails to everyone
column7: Wait until you are completely done
column10: Regular, agreed-upon updates keep everyone aligned without overload.

column4: In team meetings, one person tends to dominate the discussion. As a team member, what can you do?
column6: Invite quieter members to share their views
column10: Encouraging participation helps the team benefit from all perspectives.

column4: Your team is working with another department and roles are unclear. What should you do?
column5: Let the other department do everything
column6: Raise the issue so roles and responsibilities can be clarified and agreed
column8: Do whatever you think is needed
column10: Clarifying roles early prevents duplication and gaps.

column4: A teammate made a mistake that affects your work. What is the best response?
column5: Raise it privately and work together on a fix
column6: Ignore it and fix it yourself
column7: Point it out in front of the team
column8: Report it to the supervisor without speaking to them
column10: Addressing it privately and collaboratively maintains respect and solves the problem.

column4: Which behavior does the most to build trust within a team?
column5: Promising more than you can deliver
column10: Reliability is the foundation of team trust.

column4: Your team receives a tight deadline. What is the best first step?
column6: Agree as a team on priorities, roles and check-in points
column7: Wait for the supervisor to assign everything
column10: Shared planning focuses the team and avoids duplication.

column4: A new team member joins your group. What helps them most?
column7: Welcome them, explain how the team works and offer help
column8: Leave them to figure things out
column10: Onboarding support helps new members contribute sooner.

column4: Two teammates both want the same assignment. What is the best approach?
column6: Let the louder person have it
column8: Discuss interests and workload openly and agree on a fair split or rotation
column10: Open discussion finds fair solutions.

column4: During a team discussion, you realize your idea has a flaw a teammate pointed out. What should you do?
column5: Acknowledge the point and help improve the idea
column10: Accepting valid input improves the team's outcome.

column4: Which behavior hurts team performance most?
column5: Withholding information to look more valuable
column10: Withholding information undermines coordination.

column4: A team member is excluded from informal communication. What should you do?
column6: Include them in relevant communications and conversations
column10: Inclusion keeps everyone informed and engaged.

column4: In a virtual meeting, how can you best support collaboration?
column5: Speak over others to be heard
column8: Participate actively, share relevant updates and follow up on action items
column10: Active participation and follow-through make virtual teamwork effective.

column4: A team project failed to meet its goal. What is the most productive response?
column5: Review together what went well and what to change next time
column10: A blameless review supports learning.

column4: You finished your part of a project early. What is the best next step?
column8: Check with teammates or the lead about where help is needed
column10: Offering help moves the shared work forward.

column4: Which statement best describes 'psychological safety' on a team?
column5: Members feel safe to speak up, ask questions and admit mistakes
column10: Psychological safety enables learning and honest communication.

column10: GFCI protection is required in bathrooms and other wet or damp locations.

column10: Standard U.S. receptacles are 120 volts.

column4: Which tool is used to check whether a surface is perfectly horizontal?
column10: A level checks horizontal (and often vertical) alignment.

column4: A wall is 12 feet long and 8 feet high. How many square feet of drywall are needed to cover one side (ignoring waste and openings)?
column10: 12 x 8 = 96 square feet.

column10: Class C extinguishers are rated for energized electrical equipment.

column4: In plumbing, what does 'DWV' stand for?
column10: DWV systems carry wastewater and vent sewer gases.

column4: An HVAC filter that is dirty and clogged will most likely cause:

column10: Clogged filters restrict airflow and strain equipment.

column4: Which word correctly completes the sentence: 'Each of the employees ___ required to complete training.'

column10: Plain language uses common words and direct structure.

column4: Which transition best shows contrast?
column10: 'However' signals a contrast.

column4: When summarizing a long report for an executive, you should:
